Use Tier 2: add chronological next-item supervision to MultVAE while retaining its existing reconstruction objective and SASRec ensemble member. Focus on data_processing_and_feature_engineering, model_design, and training_evaluation. The latest ensemble scored 0.5637 macro validation HR@10, below the historical 0.6200, so another fusion adjustment has limited justification. A plausible limitation is that full-history reconstruction learns item co-occurrence without explicitly learning to predict an unseen continuation.

For each sampled training history with at least two interactions, uniformly sample a chronological cut, encode only its prefix, and use the immediately following item as the auxiliary target. Apply the existing binary normalization to that prefix and compute full-catalog next-item cross-entropy through the same VAE encoder and decoder. Optimize the original reconstruction-plus-KL loss together with 0.5 times this auxiliary loss, averaging auxiliary cross-entropy across eligible users. Keep the architecture, original reconstruction examples, SASRec training, and fusion rule unchanged to isolate this single objective change.

Use training interactions exclusively to construct prefixes, preserving all supplied splits, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR, and seed 42. Select checkpoints using validation HR@10 with fixed seed-42 candidates, and report the measured four-category macro average. Preserve the shared scoring implementation in the predictor writer and verify checkpoint reload agreement so host inference uses identical processing. This experiment tests whether explicit continuation supervision improves generalization beyond reconstructing observed preferences, without adding another inference model or accessing hidden test data.
